title: Real-time delivery: fleet_dash subscribers see every message on commit

story.i_want_to: see every message of my tenant as it lands
story.so_that: the dashboard shows the bus as it moves instead of polling it

rationale: PRD R11: fleet_dash subscribes to the message stream. The coordination-bus design chose store-and-poll and no WebSockets for agents (docs/repo-coordination-bus.md section 5), and the only socket loopctl serves outside LiveView is LoopctlWeb.RunnerSocket (lib/loopctl_web/runner_socket.ex:48), which authenticates only runner tokens (runner_socket.ex:55-101), so fleet_dash, which holds a user api key, needs a socket of its own. Waking an idle session through its machine's runner is US-52.27a, split from this story so its measurement never holds back the subscription; it computes its wakes in the after-commit step this story adds.

acceptance_criteria.description: After a message's transaction commits, Messages broadcasts {:message, summary} on the PubSub topic messages:<tenant_id>, where summary is id, attachment kind and id, attachment_seq, agent_id, author_holder_id, inserted_at and a body preview of at most 512 bytes; a rolled-back send broadcasts nothing.

LoopctlWeb.MessageSocket at /socket/messages authenticates the api key in the x-loopctl-api-key header with Loopctl.Auth.verify_api_key/1, and LoopctlWeb.MessageChannel admits a join of topic messages:tenant only for a key of role :user or above, pushing a message event per summary of that key's tenant; an :agent or :orchestrator key's join is refused with reason unauthorized.

test_cases.name: broadcast after commit only (DataCase)
steps: Messages.send/4 a message whose body fails the denylist
expected_results: one {:message, summary} with a 512-byte preview and the stored id; nothing for the refused send

test_cases.name: fleet_dash socket: user key joins, agent key refused, other tenant unseen (ChannelCase)
preconditions: user key and agent key in tenant A; user key in tenant B (test/support/channel_case.ex)
steps: connect MessageSocket with each key in x-loopctl-api-key and join messages:tenant
send a message in tenant A
expected_results: tenant A user receives one message push; agent key join {:error, %{reason: "unauthorized"}}; tenant B user receives nothing; a bad key fails connect

technical_notes: PubSub: broadcast with Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(Loopctl.PubSub, ...) after Messages.send/4's transaction returns {:ok, ...} (never inside it); the cluster carries it to the node holding each socket, as Runners.dispatch_topic/1 does (lib/loopctl/runners.ex:131, broadcast :699-716). A send deduplicated on its idempotency_key commits nothing and broadcasts nothing.

New socket because none could serve: LiveView's /live socket is browser-session-bound and RunnerSocket admits only runner tokens. Mount /socket/messages in lib/loopctl_web/endpoint.ex beside /runner/socket (:72-75) with websocket connect_info [:x_headers], longpoll false, an explicit drainer (issue #815: every socket's drainer is explicit and fly.toml kill_timeout derives from them, endpoint.ex:56-59).

The after-commit step is a function Messages calls once per committed message; US-52.27a adds the wake routing to the same step, so a message is announced to subscribers and to runners from one place.
non_goals: Waking an idle session through its machine's runner, and the measurement that picks the mechanism: US-52.27a.
The session-side hooks (SessionStart inbox block, tool-round reads) and deleting session-message.sh: US-52.28.
Keeping one machine per region running so subscriptions survive Fly suspend: release 10 (PRD R9); until then fleet_dash reconnects and re-reads.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.27.2: a fleet_dash socket cut off from loopctl misses pushes while disconnected; every message was stored before its broadcast (AC-52.27.1), so fleet_dash re-reads them through the channel and inbox reads on reconnect.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.27.1: PubSub and sockets carry only copies; the message stays in Postgres, so losing a node or a socket loses no message.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.27.1: the broadcast follows a commit, so a rolled-back send broadcasts nothing and a deduplicated retry commits and broadcasts nothing (technical_notes).
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.27.2: a slow subscriber's pushes queue in its own channel process; the sender's transaction never waits on a socket.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.27.1: the broadcast travels over the cluster's PubSub to whichever node holds each fleet_dash socket.

definition_of_done: On production, fleet_dash joined to messages:tenant with Mark's user key shows a message_send from a session within 2 s of the send.
defaults: Only :user and :superadmin keys may subscribe to messages:tenant (fleet_dash).
Body preview in a broadcast summary: at most 512 bytes.
